display.purpose: The contact close title only ("Say hi.").

hero.purpose: The single hero sentence printed on the plaster, max 12ch.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the company names in the Experience ledger.

title.purpose: Project titles, the toolbox title, the resume picker question.

subtitle.purpose: Index-line titles, "Elsewhere", the contact lead, prose h3.

body-strong.purpose: Button labels, arrow links, ledger labels, reach values.

log-message.purpose: The commit messages beside the git graph: 600 at the tips and the root, 500 in ink-soft between; 0.82rem under 480px.

log-meta.purpose: The ref or branch · date under each commit message, mono in faint ink, lime-ink at the tips; Vazirmatn 0.76rem in RTL.

caption-mono.purpose: Data only: screen captions, tags, key legends, PDF meta.

terminal.purpose: Everything printed on the terminal screen; input never under 16px on phones.

lit-display.purpose: The phone number and the email in the contact close: phosphor on glass with a bloom.

persian-display.purpose: Replaces Young Serif headings under dir=rtl (800, 1.35).

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Every legacy shadow token resolves to none; there are no drop shadows and no blur.

shadows.name: cap
shadows.purpose: Molded plastic: a 1px rim on top, a 3px skirt below. Every cap, ghost button, AI loop node, dock, chat list, resume picker.

shadows.name: cap-pressed
shadows.purpose: The cap drops 2px and its skirt collapses (90ms).

shadows.name: key-sm
shadows.purpose: Small keys: command keys, nav switches, skill keys, stack tags, kbd, Nix's speech bubble. Pressed: 2px down, 0 skirt.

shadows.name: tag-link
shadows.purpose: A linked tag is a tiny key; pressed 1px down with a 1px skirt.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: A recess the keys sit in (the AI toolbox plate).

shadows.name: screen
shadows.purpose: Glass: an inset bezel line and a rim. The terminal, browser windows, .win panels.

shadows.name: glass-band
shadows.purpose: The full-bleed contact close: bezels top and bottom.

shadows.name: glass-cap
shadows.purpose: The primary button on plastic (a glass cap with a lit label). Night: rim glass-line, skirt oklch(0.08 0.01 120).

shadows.name: lit-cap
shadows.purpose: .btn--lit and the hovered resume choice: a lime LED cap.

shadows.name: phosphor-bloom
shadows.purpose: Lit display text on glass only (contact phone and email); the neofetch host line uses 0 0 10px at 0.35. Legibility for a lit character, not elevation.

shadows.name: graph-field
shadows.purpose: The one soft field, behind the hero graph (inset 8% -10% -6% -10%); night: oklch(0.4 0.09 262 / 0.5).

shadows.name: raster-lines
shadows.purpose: The terminal's texture: a 1px line at 14% black every 4px. The only texture on the site.

shadows.name: nix-cut
shadows.value: filter: drop-shadow(1px 0 0 var(--nix-cut)) drop-shadow(-1px 0 0 var(--nix-cut)) drop-shadow(0 1px 0 var(--nix-cut)) drop-shadow(0 -1px 0 var(--nix-cut))
shadows.purpose: Nix's sticker edge: transparent on the day shell, faint bone inside .on-glass, rule-strong at night.

shadows.name: desk-edge
shadows.value: border-block-start: 2px solid var(--shell-rim); border-block-end: 1px solid oklch(0.62 0.04 84)
shadows.purpose: The 14px shell-skirt bar that closes the hero and the page; night bottom line oklch(0.08 0.01 85).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default for hover, press, entrances, the node pops, the arrival.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The lines drawing, the halos breathing, the AI loop stems, the bob.

motion.name: dur-press
motion.purpose: A cap drops 2px and its skirt collapses.

motion.name: dur-hover
motion.purpose: Colour and border hover transitions.

motion.name: dur-ui
motion.purpose: Arrow lean, LED scale, Nix head lift.

motion.name: arrival-copy
motion.value: rise 640ms ease-out, delay n * 80ms (five beats: title, lead, actions, reach, resume)
motion.purpose: The hero copy rises line by line (from 14px below).

motion.name: arrival-lines
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 -> 0 ease-in-out; main 1500ms at 250ms, armani-english 1000ms at 550ms, innolearn 800ms at 1050ms
motion.purpose: The three lanes draw themselves in chronological order.

motion.name: arrival-nodes
motion.value: scale 0 -> 1, 520ms ease-out at --at (root 150, joinArmani 800, grad 900, portal 1100, joinInno 1400, cwv 1450, innomeet 1750, head 1900)
motion.purpose: Each commit pops at its beat.

motion.name: arrival-rows
motion.purpose: Each log row slides in after its node.

motion.name: halo-breathe
motion.value: opacity 0.12 <-> 0.45, 2.8s ease-in-out infinite alternate, from --at + 600ms (no delay on a second look); paused off-screen
motion.purpose: The three buds are alive.

motion.name: arrival-land
motion.purpose: Nix drops onto HEAD.

motion.name: arrival-bubble
motion.value: scale 0.85 -> 1 (260ms) + opacity (200ms) at 2500ms, then 22ms per character
motion.purpose: His bubble scales in from its tail and types.

motion.name: nix-pose
motion.purpose: Nix's reactions to hover and focus; 14ms per character when he retypes.

motion.name: nix-lean
motion.value: rotate up to 7deg, lerp 0.14 per frame
motion.purpose: He leans toward a fine pointer; six reversals in 700ms make him panic for 1.7s.

motion.name: nix-idle
motion.value: sleep after 28s without input; a poke trick lasts 2.6s; rest returns 500ms after leaving
motion.purpose: Nix's timers.

motion.name: keystroke
motion.purpose: The toolbox keys type themselves once when first seen.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: A toolbox keycap.

motion.name: ai-loop
motion.value: step-in 420ms, delay i * 260ms; stem 300ms ease-in-out at +200ms; loop at 1300ms; then the bud walks 8 x 1.1s beats from 1.9s
motion.purpose: The AI workflow draws itself once when seen.

motion.name: browser-pan
motion.value: translate to bottom over 1.2-14s cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1) after 150ms; back in 700ms ease-out
motion.purpose: A project screenshot scrolls at reading speed on hover or focus.

motion.name: resume-open
motion.value: opacity 220ms + translate 14px 320ms ease-out (@starting-style); Nix hop 480ms at 90ms; bubble 260ms at 380ms; close 160ms ease-in
motion.purpose: The resume picker.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: Terminal carets.

motion.name: theme-circle-reveal
motion.value: view transition, clip-path circle from the toggle, 620ms ease-out (html[data-theme-switching])
motion.purpose: Day / night switch.

motion.name: page-transition
motion.purpose: Route changes.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Below-fold blocks rise into view.

motion.name: calm-path
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce or html[data-lite] or hero[data-seen]
motion.purpose: All animation off, final states visible (the graph is drawn, Nix is there); theme and page changes become a 120ms crossfade; the browser window becomes scrollable.

narrative.overview:
A software engineer's first screen is his git log. The site is built on two materials that belong to a working machine, not to a theme: sage plaster for the ground and everything you can press (caps, keys, plates, panels), and dark green-black glass for every screen (the browser windows around the shipped sites, the terminal, code blocks, the contact close). Plastic is molded: a 1px lighter rim along its top edge, a darker skirt under its bottom edge, and it drops 2px when pressed. Glass is a recess with a hairline bezel, bone text, and phosphor for whatever is alive on it. Lime is never paint; it is only ever something lit: the buds on the git graph and their breathing halos, the LEDs on plastic (the Experience buds, the "you are here" dot in the nav, a pressed key), phosphor text on glass, and the label of the one primary glass cap per block.

The first screen carries the whole idea. On one side the person: the sentence, the phone number, the email, the resume. On the other his story as a real git tree: `git init` when he was born (his photo is the root commit), a branch for studying Mechatronics that merges back when he graduated, a branch off it for Armani English, a branch for InnoLearn, three lime tips for what is alive now, growing up into his portrait: him, now. Nix stands small in the corner beside it. It grows once per session from the root up, and every commit message is a link to that part of Experience. Below it the page is compact and scannable: ruled ledgers, small screens, keycaps and index lines printed on the plaster under a chunky soft serif set large. Night is the same room under a navy sky: the shell turns navy, the glass turns navy-black and stays darker than the shell, the ink turns cool bone, and the phosphor does not change.

The world explicitly refuses: drop shadows and blur, colour gradients (the one exception is the soft radial field behind the hero graph), glow as decoration, eyebrows and kickers over headings, card grids, imitation brand marks, monospace as costume, blue or purple in the chrome, the badge + headline + CTA pair + stats hero, the neon hacker desktop, a terminal as the hero, a bone or cream ground, and any ikebana, tree or Iranian motif. This is a product, molded and quiet.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials with their own rules: sage plastic (rim on top, skirt below, pressable, ink text) and dark glass (bezel, bone text, phosphor for what is alive).
Lime is only ever lit: the graph's buds and halos, bordered LED dots on plastic, phosphor text on glass in Geist Mono, and the label of the one primary glass cap per block.
Depth is rim, skirt and recess (0-blur box-shadows), never a drop shadow; the only textures are the terminal's raster lines and the radial field behind the graph.
Young Serif 400 for the human voice on the plaster; Geist for reading; Geist Mono only where the content is literally terminal output or data (the log's refs, the neofetch, captions, tags).

One authored motion moment (the arrival: the copy rises, the tree grows from the root, one branch at a time); after it, only a quiet commit flowing up each living branch now and then. Everything else is press feedback and short state changes. Nix is still in the hero: one pose, no reactions.
Full RTL parity: logical properties, the graph and every directional pose mirrored via `--dir`, Vazirmatn 400/800 for Persian.

rules.name: The Lit, Not Painted Rule
rules.body: Lime appears only where something is lit: a bud on the graph, a bordered LED dot on plastic (Experience bud, nav "here" dot, pressed-key LED), phosphor text on glass (set in Geist Mono because it is terminal output), the label of the one primary glass cap per block, or the fill of the one lit cap on a screen. If a second thing on screen wants lime, it gets ink.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Every surface is either plastic (shell family, ink text) or glass (glass family, bone text). Text on glass is bone; anything alive on glass is phosphor. Text on plastic is ink; anything alive on plastic is lime-ink or an LED. Never bone on plastic, never ink on glass.

rules.name: The Brand-on-Hover Exception
rules.body: Tool marks sit in ink until touched: hovering a skill key lights its logo and border and tints the key 12% in the tool's own brand colour (simple-icons hex; near-black brands fall back to ink at night). The AI toolbox and AI loop marks show their real colours at rest because they are the subject there. These third-party colours are the only blues and purples on the site, and they never become UI chrome.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Every fill is a flat token. The only gradients are the terminal's raster lines (a repeating 1px line at 14% black every 4px: a texture, not a colour) and the soft radial field behind the hero graph (lime at 14% by day, `oklch(0.4 0.09 262 / 0.5)` at night, fading out at 72%). Nothing else may use one. No blue or purple in the UI.

rules.name: The Honest Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only where the content is literally terminal output or data: the log's refs and dates, the screen, the neofetch, the command keys, tags, captions, key legends, and the two lit contact lines (which are terminal output at display size). Headings, nav, buttons, prose and the log's commit messages are never mono.

rules.name: The One Weight Display Rule
rules.body: Young Serif is set at 400 with -0.015em tracking and balanced wrapping. Emphasis comes from size and position, not bold. In RTL, headings switch to Vazirmatn 800, line-height 1.35, tracking 0, and body line-height rises to 1.9.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Lists of work, skills, links and posts are rows divided by 1px hairlines (shell-line on plastic, glass-line on glass), not boxes. A row earns its height with content, not padding.

rules.name: The Log First Rule
rules.body: The hero is the person beside his graph: on desktops the words sit at the inline-start and the graph at the inline-end; on phones the words come first and the graph keeps its lane pitch underneath. The hero never becomes a badge + headline + CTA pair + stats stack, and never a terminal.

rules.name: The Rim and Skirt Rule
rules.body: Things are molded, they do not float. Depth is a 1px rim on top and a solid skirt below, and pressing a thing collapses its skirt. No drop shadows, no blur, no glow on plastic.

rules.name: The Bloom Only on Glass Rule
rules.body: The phosphor bloom exists only on lit display text on a screen. Never on plastic, never on a button label, never on body text. A bud on plastic glows by opacity (its halo), never by blur.

dos: **Do** keep lime to what is lit: the graph's buds and halos, bordered LED dots on plastic, phosphor text on glass (Geist Mono), the label of the one primary glass cap per block, the one lit cap on a screen, and transient state (selection, reading progress, a hovered resume choice); use lime-ink for any lime text or link on plastic.
**Do** put the phone number wherever the email is: navbar, hero, the close, the footer, the terminal's `contact`.

**Do** build every plastic thing as a cap: shell-lift fill, 1px shell-skirt border, a 1px rim inset on top and a solid skirt below (3px caps, 2px small keys), and make it press (2px down, skirt collapses, 90ms).

**Do** build every screen as glass: glass fill, 1px shell-skirt border, an inset glass-line bezel, 14px corners, bone text, phosphor for what is alive; put code, terminals, screenshots and the contact close on glass.

**Do** draw the graph honestly: lanes at 34 / 74 / 114 with a 64px row pitch, hollow commits for the past, lime buds only for what is alive now, the three lane colours for the lines and nothing else, and only dates `profile.ts` sources.
**Do** separate content with 1px hairlines (shell-line on plastic, glass-line on glass) and let the plaster breathe between sections (5rem); close the hero and the page with the desk edge.
**Do** use Young Serif 400 for headings and Geist for everything readable; switch both to Vazirmatn (800 for headings) in RTL, and Persian text on glass and in the log's meta too.
**Do** use logical properties and multiply every directional translate, rotate or scale by `var(--dir)`; mirror the graph, arrows and directional Nix poses in RTL.
**Do** give motion a reduced-motion and `html[data-lite]` path that shows the final state, and keep it to transform, opacity and stroke-dashoffset.
**Do** show tools by their real marks: simple-icons in currentColor (brand colour on hover), official site icons for Antigravity and Hermes Agent, or the name alone when no mark exists.
**Do** write like the person talks: first person, conversational, a little funny. Persian copy is colloquial (محاوره), not formal.
donts: **Don't** add drop shadows, blur, glow on plastic or colour gradients; depth is rim, skirt and recess, the terminal's raster lines are the only texture, and the radial field behind the hero graph is the only soft field.
**Don't** paint a surface lime, set lime body text on plastic, or bloom text anywhere but lit display text on glass.
**Don't** put an eyebrow or kicker line above a heading; a caption is for data and places only.
**Don't** build card grids; use ruled ledgers, small screens, keycaps and index lines.
**Don't** draw imitation logos or placeholder marks.
**Don't** set headings, nav, buttons or the log's commit messages in monospace to look technical; mono is for what the machine prints.
**Don't** put bone text on plastic or ink text on glass; each material keeps its own ink.
**Don't** introduce blue or purple outside the navy night shell and third-party brand marks.
**Don't** invent commits, buds or dates on the graph, and don't reuse the lane colours anywhere else.
**Don't** give a section more than one authored animation (the arrival in the hero, the loop in the AI section, the keys typing once); everything else is feedback-sized.
